column1: # The human account and token wire surface of the retired server, the old backlog
# gap 1. Earlier research records hashing, lifetimes and the cross-transport
# rule, and not one request or response shape.
# Columns: case, caller, method, path, request keys, status, set-cookie,
# response body key paths. A key path collapses an array to []. A cell of -
# means the column does not apply, and a body of - is an empty body.
# Read from a run, not from the source. The binary was built with
# `-tags "full mqtt mqttbroker observability sqlite"` and CGO_ENABLED=1 and
# started as `prusa-connect serve` against the shipped config/config.yaml
# on 2026-08-29, with auth.mode local and auth.store.type sqlite. Each row is
# one HTTP call and its answer. The walk starts on an empty ./data/auth.db.
# What the walk found that no document here said:
#   POST /api/admin/users with roles ["operator"] answers 201 and roles
#   ["viewer"]. An unknown role is taken as the lowest one rather than refused.
#   PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/roles with an empty list answers 200. An account
#   is allowed to hold no role at all.
#   DELETE on the last administrator answers 400, so an empty store is not
#   The mqtt-kind token from GET /api/account/mqtt-token is refused on HTTP with
#   401, and an api-kind token from POST /api/tokens is accepted. That is
#   earlier research's cross-transport rule, observed rather than argued.
#   The session cookie is pcl_session, Path, HttpOnly, SameSite and Max-Age
#   2592000, which is the auth.token_ttl of 720h. Logout sends the same cookie
#   GET /api/account/mqtt-token answers expires_in 43200, which is 12 hours and
